title: VPC failover conductor: staged multi-region evacuation orchestration
creator: Asha Rao
description: Build a reusable, operator-driven orchestration service ("Failover Conductor") that runs staged multi-region evacuations for Private/VPC deployments. The conductor will coordinate Terraform-based IaC actions, preflight health validations, traffic steering, and automated rollbacks. Goal: provide a safe, repeatable drill and emergency failover capability that can be executed by SRE/Platform on-call with minimal manual checklist steps and strong safety guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Conductor can perform a simulated full-region evacuation against a non-prod VPC environment with an automated rollback path
2) Terraform modules used by the conductor are idempotent and support 'dry-run' plan artifacts that the conductor can fetch and present
3) Preflight health checks (prefix KV cache sanity, token auth, probe endpoints, canary inference calls) pass before any route changes
4) Traffic shifting supports percentage-based staged rollouts with operator approval gates and timeouts
5) All run results are recorded to a central operations dashboard and a drill report is auto-generated with metrics and failed-step annotations
comments: 2026-02-12 - Design kickoff: sketched conductor responsibilities and high-level flow. Decided to implement conductor as a small Go service that orchestrates existing Terraform modules and invokes remote health checks, rather than trying to bake orchestration into Terraform alone.

2026-02-15 - Architecture review notes: PM and SRE agreed on operator approval workflow. Security requested KMS-wrapped state access and ephemeral AWS creds via STS for terraform executions (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Failover+Conductor+Design).

2026-02-20 - Prototype spike complete: PoC can call 'terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan' against the redwood-pvpc-core module and parse the plan summary. Limitations: plan parsing currently relies on 'terraform show -json' which requires terraform >=1.4; pinned to 1.5 in CI.

2026-02-26 - Safety decision: we will implement a two-step approval gate (automated preflight -> operator review -> execute). If a preflight fails, the conductor will not apply any changes and will create an incident draft in Opsgenie.

2026-03-01 - Infra review: recommended switching from ad-hoc SSH route manipulation to controlled DNS weight shifts (Route53 weighted records) combined with edge proxy connection draining for graceful handoff. Noted that some on-prem customers will require BGP path prep instead — added as a stretch goal.
2026-03-05 - Security review: mandatory audit logs for all terraform apply runs, signed S3 plan artifacts, and HSM-backed KMS for state encryption. Added labels: security-audit, kms.

2026-03-09 - Engineering update: implemented health-check harness that runs three types of probes: HTTP /healthz, model inference canary (small prompt with latency threshold), and KV cache sanity (compare cached prefix hash). Probe results are stored in /dashboards/drills/ (Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/drills/conductor).

2026-03-12 - QA: ran first non-prod rehearsal against 'pvpc-staging-us-east-1' with 5 staged shifts (10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%). Observed unexpected cache warm-up latency at 50% shift; added a pre-warm job step to the conductor before next rehearsal. Next steps: address warm-up windows and update runbook.

Reviewer feedback (Lena Patel): please add explicit snafu tests that simulate transient API token failures and ensure rollback clears half-applied terraform state. Also requested clearer runbook steps for on-call handoff. Action: add snafu scenarios to test matrix and expand runbook section titled 'Operator Playbook - Escalation and Rollback'.
